source.title: Answer-Distribution Trajectories: A Stochastic-Dynamics View of LLM Reasoning
source.authors: M. Catala; Haitz Sáez de Ocáriz Borde; D. Murari; C. Schönlieb; Pietro Liò; George D. Montañez

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies answer-distribution trajectories during chain-of-thought reasoning, not future-token representations or whether intervening on them changes intermediate text. It mentions probing future outputs only as related work.
record.gate_note: The experiments estimate answer distributions over final-answer labels from sampled continuations at reasoning prefixes. They do not probe a single hidden state for future tokens, test rhyming, or causally intervene on a future-token representation. The included rows record related findings about answer-distribution dynamics, not tests of the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study estimates final-answer distributions at chain-of-thought prefixes by Monte Carlo continuation sampling (N=16 per prefix, stride 16) across sixteen open-weight models on GSM8K, ARC, SVAMP and MATH. It never probes hidden states for future tokens and tests no rhyme planning or pre-caching. It makes no causal intervention on a planned representation. The predictive distribution pk(a) is behavioural: it marginalises over sampled future text, so it cannot show whether a single hidden state encodes future tokens (V2) or whether a plan steers generation (V5/V6). Future Lens (an original source) appears only in related work as one of several hidden-state probing papers. Relation cites_only, T6.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Answer-distribution trajectories preserve which final-answer hypotheses are supported and how support moves, beyond endpoint accuracy or entropy. Dynamics vary within and across model-task pairs, and different objectives favor different profiles. Instruction tuning, scale and temperature shift these profiles; the authors call those comparisons descriptive. They draw no conclusions about hidden-state planning.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses Monte Carlo continuation sampling from reasoning prefixes to estimate answer distributions; it does not reproduce a future-token probing or rhyme-planning method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that instruction tuning, model scale, and decoding temperature reshape trajectory metrics; the cited changes are descriptive and not tests of the listed claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Within model-task variance is the largest component for all seven trajectory metrics (e.g., S_eff within 1.09 of total 1.34).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Answer-distribution dynamics during chain-of-thought vary substantially across traces within the same model-task condition.

fits_no_version.finding: Same-question cross-model traces with similar entropy profiles can disagree on dominant answers, gold dominance and success/failure mechanism.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Entropy profiles do not identify the answer-distribution dynamics of a reasoning trace.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: AI for Stochastic Dynamics
record.problems: The reported findings are descriptive and do not causally test whether predictive information at an earlier position shapes later text. The authors state that the Section 5.3 comparisons are descriptive and that the method is computationally expensive. Figure 3 results are presented graphically, with no numerical disagreement values stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were included for endpoint-accuracy comparisons, objective-conditioned profile summaries, or training/decoding comparisons: these describe general reasoning dynamics and do not bear directly on the listed future-token planning versions.

untested.parts: No rhyming verse, no rhyme-word representations, no interventions.
No single-hidden-state probe of tokens several positions ahead; answer distributions come from sampled continuations.
No test of features computed for later positions (pre-caching/breadcrumbs).
No rhyme-planning analysis in open-weight models with attribution graphs or probes.
Multi-step math/science reasoning is studied only behaviourally via output sampling; no internal look-ahead measurement.
No assessment of plan depth or of whether internal plans steer generation.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/cites_only assignment and its all-'none' row links are confirmed. Rows are accurate but irrelevant to every version. Omitting Table 2, Figure 2 and Figure 4 is acceptable because they also bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming-verse task, candidate rhyme-word representation measurement, or intervention changing a rhyme word.
No single-hidden-state probe or measurement of token prediction several positions ahead. The study estimates final-answer distributions conditioned on text prefixes using sampled continuations.
No test of pre-caching or whether a feature is computed for later positions rather than as a side effect of next-token prediction.
No rhyme-planning test in open-weight models and no open attribution-graph or probing analysis of rhyme planning.
The evaluated tasks are GSM8K, ARC, SVAMP, and MATH; no internal look-ahead test in chess, Sokoban, or other architectures, and no causal planning intervention.
No test of whether apparent plans are shallow, incidental, heuristic, or causally steer generation.

rows.operation_detail: Compared cross-model traces for the same question with similar entropy profiles and measured disagreement in answer-distribution properties.

conditions.value: displayed range through 0.20; bins of width 0.01, with exact matches reported separately

rows.value: The text reports that even traces with similar entropy profiles can disagree about which answers are dominant; plotted percentages are figure only. RMSE range up to 0.20 is described as 12% of the largest same-question cross-model RMSE observed.
rows.locator: Figure 3 and its description in Appendix B
rows.note: The figure compares predictive answer-distribution trajectories, but does not assess hidden-state future-token representation or causal effects on intermediate text.
rows.check: Figure-only disagreement between entropy-matched cross-model trace pairs; unrelated to planning versions.
